Now that I've pretty much given up on consoles I'm looking for a way to game in my living room with my PC (I have CAT6 to my living room so bandwidth to either of these isn't a concern). I've seen a few "reviews" of these things but I was wondering if anyone here had some good first-hand experience with both of them.
Steam Link vs nVidia Shield - Anyone have experience with one or both?
nVidia is like a Roku/Xbox from what Ive read

Steam link is basically a streaming appliance. It easily and inexpensively gets games from your PC on to your living room TV. nVidia Shield is a full android device, capable of running all android apps. It also has PC game streaming but does a lot more, including nvidia's newish service GeForce Now, which is sort of like Netflix for games and doesn't require a home PC to work.

If streaming games from your PC is your only concern, get a steam link. It's cheaper, easier, and works very well. If on the other hand you want to do more, get an nVidia shield.

Ah, okay, that would explain the claims I'd heard about Shield supporting 4k while Steam Link only supports 1080p. I don't have a 4k TV yet, but prices are dropping like crazy. It'd be nice to be able to get one in a year or two without having to upgrade my streaming device as well.

Know anything about controller options with Shield? The Steam controller appears to be pretty cool but honestly I'll probably only play games in my living room that are meant to be played with a controller anyway. If I'm going to play an FPS I'll just play at my PC.
Seconding this. $50 is a great price for what the device does.
